title: LEARNING IS GOOD – A CHRISTIAN’S LIFELONG JOURNEY

memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart.” — Matthew 11:29

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
Learning is good…
Even a great person is always a student! “What we have learned is only a handful; what we have not learned is as vast as the world.” These are wise sayings of our elders. Until the day we die, we must cultivate a heart that is willing to learn something every day, because learning is pleasing to God.

When someone says, “I don’t need to learn from anyone; I know everything,” it reveals a heart that is unwilling to learn. Scripture itself teaches us to learn even from an ant, its ways and diligence (see Proverbs 6:6). Isn’t that amazing?

There are several practical ways of learning:
Formal education – to increase knowledge
Experiential learning – to grow in wisdom
Vocational learning – to increase livelihood
Spiritual education – to grow in holiness

A human being is always a learner. A man of God is both a learner and a teacher at the same time. He learns at the feet of God and communicates that truth to people. This is the highest form of education. We are called both to learn and to teach. Therefore, we must learn truth accurately. The key question is: from whom are we learning?
Mary sat at the feet of Jesus and listened to His words that was the good portion.
The apostle Paul was taught by Gamaliel, a renowned and devout Pharisee (Acts 22:3).
Because of this grounding, Paul possessed deep understanding of the Law and profound theological truth. That is why his epistles are rich in meaning and spiritual depth, continuing even today to convey the powerful truths of God.

Jesus Himself invites us to learn from Him.
Yes, even Jesus learned. He grew like us. He continually learned from the Father, listened to Him, and obeyed Him. Through suffering, He learned obedience.
“Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.”( Hebrews 5:8). This is a time when people are searching for the knowledge of truth. It is the right moment when many are seeking genuine salvation. Therefore, let us always be ready to proclaim the truth we have learned and firmly believed.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “What we learn with pleasure, we never forget.” — Alfred Mercier

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give us hearts that are eager to learn.
Remove pride from us and clothe us with gentleness and humility.
Help us to learn from You and prepare us to faithfully proclaim the truth to others.
Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Be ready not only to learn—but to boldly proclaim the truth you are convinced of.
Jesus is our glorious example: He learned, He obeyed, and He calls us to learn from Him.

recommended_book.label: Recommended Book
recommended_book.title: Knowing Scripture
recommended_book.author: R. C. Sproul
recommended_book.quote: This book strongly emphasizes learning Scripture not superficially, but deeply and responsibly. It warns that if the Bible is not approached correctly, truth itself can be misunderstood.
